dedupe_keys.name: space weather laboratory products of the university of chile

description: The Space Weather Laboratory of the University of Chile publishes real-time space weather data and visualisations in three areas: the magnetosphere (the Earth's magnetic shield and geomagnetic storms), the solar wind (interplanetary plasma flow and energetic particles) and the Sun (sunspots, flares and activity cycles). The site explains space weather and its effects on satellite lifetime, telecommunications, GPS positioning, power grid stability and radiation for air passengers, and notes that the Chilean SUCHAI I satellite was affected by a geomagnetic storm. It also has pages on the laboratory's models, researchers and publications, a glossary and a subscription, and links the Chilean Space Weather Network and the space weather pages of other Chilean universities. The site is developed under FONDEF project ID 25-10556 and showed a data update on the day it was read. Access is free online; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: the site is in Spanish, the product pages load their plots by script, and the sources of the real-time data are not listed on the page read. Coverage is global space weather, for users in Chile. It supports hazard exposure analysis of space weather for power grids, satellites and GNSS in South America; related records are the LAMP Argentine space weather laboratory and SCiESMEX of Mexico.
